- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, check for mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; apply downward bias of 3–8% in next 3–5 periods if sentiment turns negative or neutral.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., -0.28 or below), model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is negative or mixed.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply slight downward adjustment (1–3%) to first 5 forecasts if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term trends; smooth forecast curve by reducing amplitude of swings in 3–5 day windows.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops from peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in subsequent periods if sentiment is weak or negative.
